model.rationale: Harder pairs an eight-point Democratic district with a nearly 90-to-1 cash advantage and negligible outside spending against him, while Kalshi and Polymarket both price his win odds at 96 percent or higher. overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by eight points. He has raised more than $4 million and holds nearly $4.8 million in cash, while Republican John McBride has raised about $52,000 and reports under $20,000 on hand. Outside spending on either side has been negligible so far.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket put Harder's chances at roughly 96 to 98 percent. No public general-election polls are available and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. Harder also carries the standard advantages of incumbency. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves some room around the expected margin, but a genuinely competitive race would require a sharp change in the political environment.
